Hi everyone! I've been working on a website www.theoremdb.org to allow users to propose/solve math problems collaboratively.

The high level idea is a shared-workspace for LLM math, where people can pose and answer questions, along with infrastructure for formally verifying proofs. It also stores computational artifacts and "negative traces" of problems - which is something that hasn't really been possible in the math world before due to human attention constraints.

Would love feedback if folks are interested in taking a look- And if not, that's fine too!
Does this have anything to do with lean? If not then it's off-topic for this Zulip

Yes- I built in lean verification for problems as the strongest grade of evidence. I have a pool of workers on the site which run the proofs, and then sign the result.

So its an easy way to publish and share lean proofs instead of needing someone to go to a github repo.

example:
https://theoremdb.org/statements/fib-problem-determinant-range/#lean-verification
My goal was to make it really easy to pose problems for others to solve and verify, and I was planning to use lean to do that.
